aiAnalysis.rootCause: The login step completed without an explicit error, but the post-login assertion could not find any authenticated-user UI markers. The most likely cause is that the test is checking outdated or incorrect selectors for the signed-in state, or the app now renders a different authenticated shell than the smoke test expects. A secondary possibility is that the credentials/session setup no longer produces a real authenticated session, but the absence of any login error makes a selector mismatch the strongest hypothesis.
aiAnalysis.suggestion: Update the smoke test to verify authentication using a stable source of truth, such as a session cookie, API-authenticated endpoint, or a single canonical user-profile element maintained for automation. If the UI has changed, refresh the authenticated-state selectors and confirm the test credentials still log in successfully in the target environment.

aiInsights: The test run is not acceptable: 1 of 1 cases failed, resulting in a 0% pass rate and a quality score of 39/100, which indicates low confidence in the current build. With no passing coverage in this run, the defect appears unresolved and the build should not be considered release-ready until the failure is identified and fixed.
The run appears narrowly focused: there was only one failure, so this is likely a targeted smoke-test issue rather than a broad system outage.
The failure happens after form submission, which points to a post-auth verification problem instead of a basic navigation failure.
The test relies on several brittle DOM selectors for authentication state, which makes it sensitive to UI changes.
Saving browser state succeeded, so the setup/auth capture phase did not hard-fail; the break is in validation logic after login.
Reliability would improve by replacing UI-only auth detection with a more stable check and by keeping a dedicated automation hook for signed-in state.
